target_name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
rationale: A clean, well-motivated single-ratio ablation of the two winning composites, and the industry adjustment is justified since current-liability intensity is sector-driven, though EBITDA-to-current-liabilities is close to standard distress/coverage screens (Beaver-style cash-flow-to-debt) and unwinding the rank-product may simply reintroduce the outlier sensitivity that ranking was there to control.

Internally consistent and a legitimate complementarity-versus-redundancy test of the two independently successful legs with equalized weighting, but it is an incremental merge of two archive winners whose result is likely to sit mechanically between the parents, so its diagnostic value hinges entirely on the leg correlation being reported alongside the alpha.

This is a cosmetic three-year-smoothing variant of the archive's best signal, and the archive already contains two cases where MA-smoothing the profitability leg (Profits Not Propped By New Debt, Stable Financing Durable Profits) collapsed alpha to roughly zero, so the prior on smoothing helping here is weak and the design choice has effectively been tested.

The stated mechanism is an externally priced implied borrowing rate, but xint/lt is dominated by the interest-bearing share of the liability stack rather than by the rate charged, so the expression largely recomputes the debt-mix channel already captured by dlc/lt while the hypothesis claims a distinct information source.

The conjunctive logic is coherent and the control is clean, but MIN of two uniform ranks is very highly correlated with their product, so this is a near-cosmetic functional-form variant of the parent with little expected incremental information and added tie/compression problems in the extreme buckets.

The sales-benchmarked current-liability growth leg is the batch's only genuinely new flow mechanism and is economically sensible, but note the direction contradicts the working-capital accrual anomaly (rising current liabilities lower accruals, which Sloan associates with higher future returns) and lct growth is strongly correlated with total asset growth, so the test must control for both to be interpretable.
